summary: Discovery call to validate Stonemere's private deployment requirements: VPC peering, private endpoints, region constraints, and an on-prem option for regulated data. Primary concerns: egress controls, network ACLs, KMS/HSM integration, and whether Dedicated or Private (on‑prem) makes sense for latency and compliance. Redwood AE/SE confirmed support for transit gateway peering, private endpoints, SOC2/KMS integrations; proposed next steps: network diagram, perf plan, security questionnaire and follow-up demo for on-prem package.
topics: On-prem deployment options and air-gap needs
KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
Latency vs cost tradeoffs and Dedicated capacity
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Emily Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Jenna Liu (Network Lead - Stonemere), Rao Patel (CTO), Maya Singh (Security), Anil (Infra Eng)

[00:00] Emily (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Emily, i'm the AE on this account. carlos here is our solutions engineer. how's everybody doing?
[00:10] Jenna (Stonemere): doing well, thanks. quick heads up, we've got a tight window — compliance team wants an architecture review by end of month.
[00:16] Rao (Stonemere CTO): yup, want to understand hosting options — hosted, dedicated, private on-prem — but must be clear on network boundaries and egress.
[00:24] Carlos (Redwood SE): great, today we want to map requirements and see what fits. we support hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and two private flavors: VPC-hosted private endpoints and a customer-managed on-prem bundle.
[00:36] Maya (Security): i'd like to jump in on encryption and key mgmt — do you integrate with customer KMS or HSM?
[00:42] Emily: yes, we support KMS integrations, customer-managed keys for private deployments; for hosted there's an option for customer-managed keys in specific plans, we can share the security docs.
[00:53] [speaker 3]: (inaudible)
[00:56] Anil (Infra Eng): can you explain how VPC peering works — our current architecture uses a transit gateway in AWS, multiple accounts, and we prefer not to punch holes to the public internet.
[01:05] Carlos: absolutely. for our private endpoint mode we either set up VPC peering or use transit gateway attachments depending on scale. with transit gateway you can centralize peering to a single TGW; we also support PrivateLink style private endpoints — effectively AWS interface endpoints in your VPC so traffic never traverses the public internet.
[01:25] Jenna: so PrivateLink is preferred, but our security team also asks about egress IPs for allowlisting with external data providers. can you guarantee stable egress ranges?
[01:34] Emily: for Dedicated and Private we can provide a set of egress IP ranges per region. Hosted is more dynamic, but we do publish egress ranges for enterprise customers and can arrange static NAT in some setups.
[01:46] Rao: what's the difference in latency if we go Private via VPC peering vs on-prem?
[01:50] Carlos: on-prem can actually be lower latency if you colocate the model serving near your applics, but it depends on your network topology. VPC peering/PrivateLink to our managed nodes in a co-located region usually gives single-digit to mid-double-digit ms for inference, whereas an on-prem box has fixed network hops but you control everything.
[02:11] Maya: compliance — SOC2, ISO — do you provide audit logs for inference requests and KMS key usage logs?
[02:18] Emily: yes, we surface audit logs, token-level tracing, and KMS integration events. we'll share the SOC2 report and our security pack.
[02:24] [00:02:30] Speaker 4: is there a limit to number of VPCs that can peer?
[02:35] Carlos: it's largely bounded by cloud provider limits; transit gateway scales better for many VPCs. for 1-5 accounts peering may be fine; beyond that TGW or a vendor-managed peering mesh is recommended.
[02:47] Jenna: our data residency requirement — some data must remain in eu-west-1. can you pin model instances to a region?
[02:53] Carlos: yes, customers can pin model versions and serving clusters to specific regions. our Private control plane can be deployed in your region for full residency.
[03:05] Rao: what about KV cache and prefix caching — does that sit in our VPC or in Redwood? can we control caching to avoid storing sensitive prefixes?
[03:13] Carlos: good question. the KV cache is part of the serving runtime; for private deployments the cache can be hosted in your VPC or on-prem so you control retention. in hosted mode the cache is managed but we provide TTL controls and don't persist raw customer PII by default.
[03:32] [00:03:40] Jenna: any extra network components we need? subnets, route tables, NACLs?
[03:38] Emily: we'll provide a network checklist: required subnets (private), route table entries to TGW or ENIs for interface endpoints, security group rules for ports, and guidance on NACLs. we'll send the template after the call.
[03:52] Anil: about DNS — will you require us to manage split-horizon DNS for private endpoints?
[03:57] Carlos: we support both approaches. you can use your private zone and map a record to the interface endpoint, or we can provision DNS records inside your VPC if you prefer. some customers use Route53 private hosted zones and that's straightforward.
[04:11] Maya: does your private package support air-gapped installs for regulated workloads?
[04:16] Emily: yes, there's an on-prem kit — it's a customer-managed binary and runtime that can be deployed behind your firewall. in that mode we do an initial bootstrap, then the control plane can be operated in air-gapped fashion with offline licensing. we'll need to run through the installer checklist.
[04:29] Rao: curious about upgrades — if we run on-prem, how do you handle patching and kernel updates to models?
[04:34] Carlos: upgrades are coordinated; we ship a versioned artifact and you can run in staging first. we also support a canary rollout pattern and you can pin to a version. for security patches we recommend a scheduled maintenance window.
[04:45] [00:05:00] Unknown (Finance): (mumbles about pricing) is dedicated a flat rate or usage?
[04:52] Emily: Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract — monthly/annual commit with a baseline and optional overage rates. Hosted is usage-based. We'll attach a pricing comparison doc.
[05:03] Jenna: on the networking side, we're particularly concerned about egress controls to 3rd-party data vendors — do you support NAT gateway with fixed egress?
[05:12] Carlos: yes for private deployments you can set up NAT or a fixed egress via a NAT or static IP appliance; we can also support sourcing egress from your own NAT so logs show your source IPs.
[05:23] Emily: quick note — some customers route all model traffic through a proxy for DLP inspection; we support that pattern.
[05:30] [00:05:40] Carlos: technical note — if you want low token cost we suggest quantized model variants; those can run on dedicated GPUs or on-prem boxes. there might be a small latency increase depending on quantization, we can test.
[05:44] Rao: what network bandwidth do you recommend per concurrent client?
[05:48] Carlos: it depends on payload size and request rate. for typical chat traffic, 1-3 Mbps per concurrent realtime client is often sufficient; we'll include sample numbers in the perf plan.
[05:58] Jenna: are there any special IAM roles to create?
[06:01] Emily: yes we'll provide a least-privilege IAM template for the cross-account role or the service link role required to attach to your TGW or to provision interface endpoints.
[06:12] Anil: have you run into problems with corporate proxies and certificate inspection?
[06:16] Carlos: some customers with TLS interception need to whitelist our certs or run a TLS passthrough. for private endpoints the traffic is inside the VPC and simpler.
[06:28] [00:06:40] Maya: we need to know about logging retention — how long do you keep request logs and audit trails?
[06:34] Emily: default retention is 90 days for traces; extended retention is available as an add-on. in private/on-prem you can configure retention to comply with your policy.
[06:44] Jenna: do you have a compliance questionnaire or security whitepaper?
[06:47] Emily: yes, we'll share an updated security pack, SOC2, encryption details, and the KMS integration guide.
[06:54] [00:07:00] Carlos: would you prefer we walk through a sample network diagram now or send the template?
[07:03] Rao: send the template first and then we can sketch and set a follow-up to review.
[07:08] Carlos: ok, quick perf question — do you plan to use our hosted API or are you leaning fully private?
[07:14] Jenna: leaning private due to data residency; might run a hybrid where non-sensitive workloads use hosted.
[07:20] Carlos: that's common. hybrid gives you quick time-to-value while moving regulated workloads to private clusters.
[07:27] [00:07:40] Emily: any blockers from procurement or legal we should know?
[07:31] Unknown (Finance): we need standard msft legal SLA and indemnities — procurement will send redlines.
[07:36] Maya: and we need to ensure HSM-backed keys for certain datasets.
[07:40] Carlos: HSM integration is supported for private deployments; for hosted we have options but may require an enterprise plan.
[07:48] Jenna: about regions — we operate in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 primarily; can we keep data in eu-west-1 for a subset of workloads?
[07:55] Emily: yes, model pins and regional clusters allow that. we'll note region constraints in the proposed design doc.
[08:03] [00:08:20] Anil: do you provide sample Terraform to create endpoints and route tables?
[08:08] Emily: yes, we provide Terraform modules and CloudFormation examples for the major cloud providers.
[08:14] Rao: curious about network observability — can we see per-request latency and which node served it?
[08:19] Carlos: yes, our console exposes per-route/model dashboards, per-token latency breakdowns, and trace ids you can ingest into your APM.
[08:28] [00:08:40] Jenna: one more — what about cross-region replication for model artifacts? if we host eu data in eu-west-1, will model weights be pulled from us?
[08:36] Carlos: we keep model artifacts localized for private clusters; for hosted models there's replication but for residency-sensitive setups we deploy artifacts into the target region or your on-prem storage so nothing leaves the region.
[08:49] Maya: ok, lock on that.
[08:51] [00:09:00] Emily: wrap up — we'll send: network checklist, security pack, pricing comparison, and a perf test plan. any final questions?
[09:00] Jenna: timing — can you get the docs by Friday?
[09:03] Emily: yes, we'll aim for 2026-04-17.
[09:07] Rao: after that we'll schedule a technical deep dive with our infra and security teams.
[09:11] Carlos: sounds good.
[09:13] [00:09:20] Speaker 1 (inaudible):
[09:18] Emily: thanks everyone, meeting notes will be posted and I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[09:25] Jenna: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and inaudible segments noted; some speakers abbreviated. references shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (security pack link), https://redwood.example.com/network-template (network diagram template), pricing_comparison_v2.pdf (internal link).
